chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Salim al-Ashall, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the game hunted by a trained dog that had eaten from its catch, and he said: 'Eat from it.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع: Abu Abdillah (the Imam), peace be upon him

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat from game hunted by a dog that ate some of it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of consuming game hunted by a trained dog, even if the dog consumes part of the catch before retrieval. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that the dog's eating does not render the meat *najis* or impermissible, provided the dog was sent with the owner's name mentioned, distinguishing it from general hunting rules. It underscores the practical flexibility in Islamic dietary laws regarding wild game, emphasizing the condition of the dog's training and the owner's invocation over the physical act of consumption by the animal.
